consumer_audit.scope: Read-only audit of direct mutable conversion and mutable arithmetic call sites in the current reader, pinned DataFusion 54.1.0, its local dependency patches, Sail and Arrow 58.4.0. This does not cover arbitrary external consumers or future dependency versions.
consumer_audit.conclusion: No current SQL Decimal consumer was identified that gains an additional mutable-conversion copy from this owner. The public into_mutable/into_vec limitation remains. Retained output disables the global reuse slot until its last reference drops.

sources.finding: Buffer::into_mutable and into_vec reject custom deallocation; this is a real public Arrow ownership limitation.
convert_to_state uses binary_mut on its freshly allocated initial_state; the input values are only the borrowed right operand.
Mutable builders consume UInt64/UInt32 join indices, not Decimal value buffers.
into_data().into_builder() changes ArrayData null-mask metadata; it does not request mutable value allocation.
Nested NULL mask repair rebuilds ArrayData metadata, retaining value buffers.
Numeric operations use borrowed unary/try_unary/binary/try_binary kernels, rather than consuming the input through mutable kernels.
The currently patched round_columnar uses borrowed array traversal kernels.
scatter_updates reads base/update ArrayData into a newly allocated MutableArrayData; it does not reclaim the input value buffer.
Dictionary casts rebuild ArrayData metadata from cast integer keys and attach the cast values. They do not reclaim mutable Decimal value buffers.

findings: Earlier results no longer exclude later conversions from reuse: all eligible allocations may return to the single idle slot on final release. The slot holds only released memory.
With one retained SQL batch, slow target processes fall from 5/24 to 0/24 in this run. Across all four modes, no candidate target process is high-fault (0/96).
The no-retention SMALLINT median is 1.50% higher; released is 0.68% higher. The unchanged Decimal control is 0.10-0.59% higher. These observations do not establish zero overhead.
Four-worker retained-output median falls from 7.567 ms with the global gate to 3.583 ms with thread-local idle buffers; 6 processes each. No concurrency penalty appears in this measured workload.
The runtime helper including tests shrinks from 240 to 208 lines; no new dependency or Python runtime code.
limitations: Idle storage is bounded at 256 KiB plus metadata per OS thread, no longer per process. Live results and allocator retention are outside that bound.

Cross-thread final release populates the receiving thread cache, which is freed on thread exit. A producer/consumer thread split can reduce reuse; arbitrary task migration and Python C Stream throughput were not benchmarked.

Every eligible output now has custom ownership, including overlapping outputs. External consumers requiring into_mutable/into_vec still cannot reclaim it directly. The unchanged source audit found no additional copy in current SQL consumers.
Measurements cover the recorded Linux/glibc host, selected workloads and batch sizes, not universal performance.
